propositions: On platforms without /proc, _process_start_time always returns None, making the recycled-pid discriminant unsatisfiable and allowing dead processes with recycled pids to hold locks unboundedly
When a live-pid branch has current_start unavailable (None), the ceiling backstop is now applied to bound the hold time, whereas previously the check was skipped
A process with matching stamped and current start times is never reclaimed on a timer, preserving the invariant that a genuinely live owner holding the fcntl leg cannot be broken
The owner-identity, stamp, staleness, and reclaim logic was extracted into lock_owner.py to fit within the 800-line module-size limit while preserving one-way dependency and fixing the bug

The fix is conservative because a reclaimer reaching _mkdir_lock_is_stale must have acquired the exclusive fcntl leg, proving the stamped owner released it, so the ceiling only fires on orphaned locks
